title: fix(metadata-fs, runtime): an actor-less filesystem write records null, never the label fs; the dispatcher metadata PUT records the user
body:
Part of #23086
Clause-②: no

This PR covers positions 2 and 3 of the `PutOptions.actor` producer family. The contract (`packages/metadata-core/src/types.ts`, #4556) is the acting user's id, or `null`, and never a label. It follows the triage direction in comment 6131584326: positions 2 and 3 in one PR, one pin per position, no second resolver, and no new repo-wide check. Position 1 (plugin-security's `'system'`) is not edited here. The card stays open so the seat can verify position 1 when #22975's 7a and 7b land.

## Measured first, on `origin/main` `6662e3f590`

- **Position 1, confirmed and not edited.** Both modules still pass the label. `permission-set-projection.ts:1658` has `actor: 'system'`, and so does `position-environment-backfill.ts:299`. The same two hits are there at `9956048b4c` and at `origin/main` `8464380248`.
- **Position 2: where `'fs'` lands.** `FileSystemRepository`'s constructor set `this.fsActor = opts.fsActor ?? 'fs'`, and `fsActor` reached four places:
  - the event `actor` of an edit seen on disk (`handleFsChange`, `publishExternalDelete`);
  - `authoredBy` in `get()`, in the `list()` header, and in a no-op `put()`, each spelled `meta?.actor ?? this.fsActor`.

  `??` treats a recorded `null` as absent. So a `put()` with `actor: null` read back from `get()` / `list()` as authored by `'fs'`, even though the write and its log record held `null`. The new pin read exactly that on the unfixed source: `expected { get: 'fs', list: [ 'fs' ], … } to deeply equal { get: null, list: [ null ], … }`.
- **`MetadataPlugin` never passes `fsActor`.** `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts` constructs the repository with `root`, `org` and `disableWatch` only, so every host that boots the plugin inherited the label.
- **Readers of `authoredBy` and the event actor from this repository: none key on `'fs'`.**
  - `MetadataManager.applyRepoEvent` reads `op`, `ref`, `ts` and `seq`, and never `actor`.
  - `MetadataManager.getRepository()` has no non-test caller.
  - No HTTP route exposes this repository's history or items, and the HMR legacy events carry no actor, so no Studio provenance display can read it.
  - `LayeredRepository` is never constructed over it outside tests.
  - In non-test `packages/**/*.ts`, a `git grep` finds no comparison of an actor or `authoredBy` with `'fs'`.
  - The only readers keyed on the label were nine assertions in `metadata-fs`'s own watcher suites (`expect(… .actor).toBe('fs')`). They are updated below.
  - `fsActor` itself has no producer anywhere in this tree.
- **Position 3.** `HttpDispatcher`'s `PUT /metadata/:type/:name` branch called `saveMetaItem` with no `actor`, although the execution context it had just admitted carries `userId`. A signed-in author's save through the `@objectstack/hono` catch-all therefore recorded `null` in `sys_metadata.updated_by` / `created_by` and `sys_metadata_history.recorded_by`. The new pin read exactly that on the unfixed branch: `expected { created_by: null, … } to deeply equal { created_by: 'u_author', … }`. `RestServer`'s twin records the user through `resolveMetaWriteActor`.

## Change

- `packages/metadata-fs/src/repository.ts`:
  - `fsActor` defaults to `null`, and its exported type (`fsActor?: string`) is unchanged. Its doc now states the rule: a user id for a change the repository did not write itself, `null` when omitted, never a label. `source: 'fs'` already names the origin on every event.
  - The three `authoredBy` reads go through one private `authoredByOf(meta)`. When a log record exists, it answers with that record's actor, and a recorded `null` stays `null`. Only when no record exists (a file placed on disk outside the repository) does it answer with `fsActor`.
- `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`: a comment at the attach states the actor rule, as the explicit-composition rule asks. The code is unchanged. With the default gone, the attach gives `null`.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts`: the `PUT` branch passes `executionContext.userId` when it is a non-empty string, and nothing otherwise. That is the same inline reading the `_migrate-stored` branch got in `8c10776152`, with no new resolver function. The actor is read off the admitted identity only, never off `item` or a header.
- `.changeset/23086-actor-family.md`: `patch` for `@objectstack/metadata-fs` and `@objectstack/runtime`, written for an operator. `@objectstack/metadata` is not listed because its only change is a `//` comment, and no comment ships. Built `packages/metadata/dist` holds zero hits for the new comment and zero for the pre-existing comment above it, in js, cjs and maps. The positive control, the runtime string `FileSystemRepository attached`, hits `dist/index.js` once.

## Pins (one per position, plus the control)

- **Position 2, the repository:** `packages/metadata-fs/test/actor-never-a-label.test.ts` (new). It checks the `put()` receipt, `get()`, the `list()` header and the `history()` event:
  - a write with no actor records `null` on every surface, a no-op rewrite included;
  - a write by `usr_alice` records `usr_alice` on every surface;
  - a file no recorded write produced reports `null`;
  - a named `fsActor` answers only where no write is recorded, and a recorded `null` stays `null`.

  The nine watcher-suite assertions now read `actor` as `null` for an edit seen on disk (`source` still `'fs'`).
- **Position 2, the `MetadataPlugin` door:** `packages/metadata/src/plugin-fs-repository-actor.test.ts` (new). A real `LiteKernel` boots a real `MetadataPlugin`, and the test reads the repository handle it attached. A file placed under `.objectstack/metadata` before boot reports `null`, and so does an actor-less `put()`. The positive control is that the placed file was indexed. If a future attach passes a label as `fsActor`, this test turns red.
- **Position 3, the dispatcher door:** `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-save-actor.test.ts` (new). Each door gets its own real store: better-sqlite3 `:memory:`, the real `sys_metadata*` objects, and a real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`. The test reads the rows back after every save:
  - a signed-in `u_author` save records `u_author` in `created_by`, `updated_by` and `recorded_by`;
  - a later save by `u_editor` moves `updated_by` to `u_editor`, keeps `created_by`, and appends `u_editor` to `recorded_by`;
  - an `isSystem` save with no user records `null` in all three.

  An anonymous caller never reaches the save, because the anonymous deny answers first, so "nobody" is the `isSystem` caller.
- **CONTROL:** the same two cases run against `RestServer`'s `PUT` twin (`resolveMetaWriteActor`), which is unchanged and records the same rows.
- `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.test.ts`: the deliberate exact-match pin of the dispatcher's `saveMetaItem` request now includes `actor: 'u1'`. It was the one red in the full runtime run before that update.

## Ablation

The fix and its pins were committed first. Each leg went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, which carries its own restore trap. The legs ran inside one script that also carried an `EXIT INT TERM` trap restoring both files from `HEAD` by absolute path. The run was at `1f9c123dcf`.

- **Leg A1, the `'fs'` default restored** (`opts.fsActor ?? null` back to `opts.fsActor ?? 'fs'`):
  - The anchor fell from 1 to 0 and the blob went from `f76f6dee4f48` to `bfde62909356`.
  - `metadata-fs` was rebuilt, and `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` found the marker in 2 built files. The pristine witness had found the fixed spelling in dist before the mutation.
  - Result: `metadata-fs` 11 failed and 63 passed. The failures were the new pin's file-with-no-record case and the ten watcher tests behind the nine updated assertions (`expected 'fs' to be null`). The new pin's other three cases stayed green.
  - The plugin door pin failed 1 of 1 (`expected 'fs' to be null`). The runtime pin passed 4 of 4.
  - Restore leg: rebuilt, and the preflight found the marker absent from all 6 built files with the tree clean.
- **Leg A2, the `meta?.actor ?? this.fsActor` fallback restored, with the default left `null`:**
  - The anchor fell from 1 to 0 and the blob went from `f76f6dee4f48` to `c50311af3a10`.
  - Result: `metadata-fs` 1 failed and 73 passed. The failure was the named-`fsActor` case, `expected { get: 'usr_operator', … } to deeply equal { get: null, … }`. The runtime pin passed 4 of 4.
  - The plugin pin was not run in this leg: its subject resolves through `metadata-fs`'s `dist/`, which this leg did not rebuild, so its reading would have proved nothing.
- **Leg B, the dispatcher's `userId` dropped** (`const actor: string | undefined = undefined;`):
  - The anchor fell from 1 to 0 and the blob went from `84a24c33019f` to `5632faa44578`.
  - Result: the runtime pin had 1 failed and 3 passed. The failure was the dispatcher's signed-in case, `expected { created_by: null, … } to deeply equal { created_by: 'u_author', … }`. The dispatcher's `isSystem` case and both `RestServer` control cases stayed green.
  - The `metadata-fs` pin (4/4) and the plugin pin (1/1) stayed green.
- **Restore:** both blobs equal `HEAD` (`f76f6dee4f48`, `84a24c33019f`). `git diff HEAD` is empty and `git status --porcelain` is empty.

## Verification

`origin/main` `55828c5145` was merged once, at `9956048b4c`. The runtime and metadata-fs changes are disjoint from it. After the merge I ran `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `turbo run build --filter=!@objectstack/docs` (73/73 tasks).

- At `9956048b4c`:
  - `@objectstack/metadata-fs` `pnpm test`: 11 files, 74 tests, exit 0.
  - `@objectstack/metadata` `pnpm test`: 61 files, 880 tests, exit 0.
  - `@objectstack/runtime` `--project local` over `src/http-dispatcher.test.ts` and `src/domains/`: 110 files, 2299 tests, exit 0.
  - `typecheck` for `metadata-fs`, `metadata` and `runtime`: exit 0. Runtime's test-typecheck ledger is unchanged (27 files, 190 errors, 68 pinned signatures).
- Before the merge, at `f489836584`, `@objectstack/runtime`'s full `--project local` suite ran 362 files: 361 passed, and 1 failed. The failure was the exact-match pin in `http-dispatcher.test.ts`, updated in `1f9c123dcf`. 5166 tests passed and 19 were skipped. The full runtime suite was not re-run after the merge. The incoming commits touch `metadata-protocol`'s envelope and install-lock paths, not the save actor path, so only the meta domain, the dispatcher file and the pins were re-run. The merge ref's full run is CI's.
- **Gates, at the final head `9956048b4c`:** `dispatch-gates --commands` derived 66 commands on the real diff. That is the 55-command lead list plus 11 changeset-family commands. Each exit code was captured before any pipe, and all 66 exited 0. `dispatch-gates --ran` reports 66 derived, 66 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED and 0 UNRUN.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` read real built output after a full build (107 entries, 66 packages).
  - `check:query-options-erasure` is back at its 236-site test ceiling.
  - The derivation warns that `origin/main` has since moved by 2 commits, which changed three engine-double roster baselines. This diff adds no engine double.
- **Lint, a proven narrowing:** `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 14 changed `.ts` files gives 14 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 ignore notices, so all 14 were linted. `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting (its own comment at line 327: no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules), so this diff cannot change the verdict on any file it does not touch. The repository-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- Entries written before this release keep what they recorded: `'fs'` in an existing `.objectstack/.log/main.jsonl`, and `null` in dispatcher-saved rows. This is per the card's "Not here".
- `fsActor` has no producer in this tree. Retiring it would narrow an exported options type (Clause-② narrowing). It is left in place with its type unchanged, and only its default moved. No card is filed: per the family rule, this is an observation and not a defect.
- `RestServer.resolveMetaWriteActor`'s docblock (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`) still says "the protocol's `'system'` / `NULL` defaults still apply". The `'system'` half has been stale since #4556. The file is outside this claim, and nobody is carrying it.
- The dispatcher `PUT`'s fallback, `metadata.saveItem(type, name, item)`, carries no actor either. No metadata service in this tree implements `saveItem` (the only hits are the client SDK's `meta.saveItem`), so the branch is unreachable with the in-tree `MetadataManager`. This is a dead-code observation, not filed.
- A dispatcher save by a signed-in user now also gets that user in `sys_metadata_audit.actor` (through `recordMetadataAudit`) instead of that column's `'system'` default, the same as on the REST door.
- Comments in `metadata-fs`'s `self-write-suppression.test.ts` that quote the pre-fix symptom `{op:'update', actor:'fs'}` are left as the historical record of what was measured.
